observations.observation: The earliest traceable Reuters Events listing for the report is dated 2026-09-28; a Reuters-attributed full-text syndication on the same date describes data-center developers seeking small open-cycle and aeroderivative turbines for BTM generation and quicker power access. The report does not identify Bloom or a project previously associated with Bloom.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: Exact hour is unknown; the direct Reuters Events page was inaccessible. The 2026-09-29 Reuters.com record supplied in the case is after cutoff and is not used.

observations.observation: Before the Reuters coverage, Enverus had published the core forecast: 29.6 GW is gas-generation capacity needed, while 88% refers to data centers’ share of 25.5 GW projected BTM demand (22.5 GW).
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: These are forecasts, not completed builds or Bloom allocations. Enverus also describes project readiness risks including permits, pipeline routes, water, community acceptance, and offtakers.

observations.observation: Enverus’s August 2026 public analysis had already described modular gas and fuel cells as faster alternatives to large CCGTs and forecast they could capture a substantial share of planned gas builds; it also presented SOFCs as a competing BTM technology.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This was an industry forecast, not proof of realized customer adoption or a specific technology’s share at any Bloom-related site.

observations.observation: Crusoe’s 29-unit GE Vernova aeroderivative-turbine order was publicly announced in July 2025: 19 units booked in June 2025 and 10 previously ordered in December 2024. The September 2026 report repeats an already disclosed transaction.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The company described expected capacity and supply; the release does not establish that all turbines had been delivered or commissioned.

observations.observation: Bergen’s June 2026 announcement of a roughly 750 MW Crusoe agreement split the amount into approximately 438 MW of contract and 310 MW of LOI, with delivery phased through 2027.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: An LOI is not the same evidentiary status as contracted capacity; the announcement does not prove delivery or operation by the cutoff.

observations.observation: The Reuters-attributed report itself included counterpoints: it reported that smaller turbines can have higher capital cost per unit of electricity, while larger CCGTs can have lower lifetime costs and emissions per MWh; it also described batteries, hybrid resources, grid enhancements, and efficiency as alternatives.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: These are attributed estimates and views, not project-specific comparisons; they do not identify the route chosen for a Bloom-associated project.

observations.observation: Manufacturing responses were already public before cutoff: GE Vernova announced a Greenville expansion plan in January 2025, and Mecklenburg County reported in February 2026 that Siemens Energy planned to resume gas-turbine manufacturing in Charlotte.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: Announcements and future expansion do not establish additional turbine output available by the cutoff.

gaps: The Reuters Events original page returned an access error, and the earliest traceable listing establishes the publication date but not the exact publication hour or a dated archived text snapshot.
The case-provided Reuters.com record is later than cutoff; it was excluded. The accessible same-day Reuters syndication is dated 2026-09-28 but has no time-of-day or update marker.

No located source identifies a Bloom-associated project that switched from Bloom to gas turbines, gives a Bloom-specific lost order, or quantifies comparative deployment economics for a named project.
Forecasts and announced supply transactions do not establish realized BTM additions, turbine deliveries, commissioning, or technology allocation by the cutoff.
research_notes: Cutoff: 2026-09-29T09:26:01.472751Z. The earliest traceable listing found for Neil Ford’s Reuters Events story is dated 2026-09-28; the full Reuters-attributed text also appears on Pipeline & Gas Journal with that date. Neither shows an hour. The Reuters Events page could not be fetched, so its listing is used only to trace dissemination. The case-provided Reuters.com record is dated 2026-09-29 with a 16:00Z publication value, after cutoff, and is not used as evidence. Enverus had already published the principal BTM forecast and modular-technology context before the Reuters coverage. Its figures distinguish 29.6 GW of gas generation capacity from 25.5 GW of BTM demand, of which data centers account for 22.5 GW (88%). Crusoe’s 29-turbine order and Bergen agreement were also publicly disclosed earlier. No located source identifies a Bloom-associated project switching routes or a Bloom-specific order change.
